raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not want to spread the work too wide or take big risks. Cotton is still my main crop because I know how to manage it, but I also keep some wheat-maize land because that is steady and gives more secure grain and cash. With only two people in the house, I have to keep the plan practical: not too much hired labor, fertilizer at a level I can afford, and irrigation only at the important stages because pumping from the well costs money.

For the wheat-maize land, I will mostly follow what has worked on my fields before. Wheat needs enough base fertilizer and at least a few irrigations, otherwise yield drops too much. Maize after wheat has a very tight window, so I will keep tillage simple and plant quickly after harvest. For cotton, I will not push the fertilizer too hard; cotton can make money, but it also takes labor, especially later in the season, so I will keep the area at a level I can still manage. If pests are light, I will spray only when I really see a problem.
